checks_performed: Read only the specified input JSON and used no web sources.
Checked all Euler, degree, face-perimeter, parity, and component-count identities with integer arithmetic.

Created face_switch_checker.py in the scratch directory. It checks cubicity, bipartiteness, all vertex cuts of size at most two, the supplied spherical face incidence certificate, proper face 3-colouring, auxiliary forests, and resulting 2-factors. Tests on even prisms of orders 8, 12, 16, 20, and 24, including spanning trees requiring up to five switches, produced verified Hamiltonian cycles.

Created and ran small_order_obstruction_check.py. It enumerated all relevant integer face profiles through order 30 and all 512 labelled bipartite graphs on parts of size 3. Exactly nine 8-edge graphs and one 9-edge graph had feedback-vertex number at least two; these are the nine copies of K_{3,3} minus one edge and K_{3,3}. All assertions passed.
final_writeup:
No full resolution or counterexample is claimed; the supplied paper itself describes the target as widely open. The main rigorous progress is a collection of constructive reductions and a self-contained small-order theorem.

For the canonical proper 3-colouring of the faces, each colour class gives a facial spanning 2-factor. Quadrilateral faces of another colour define an auxiliary graph; a spanning forest in it can be converted explicitly into a spanning 2-factor having exactly one cycle per auxiliary component. Consequently, connectivity of this auxiliary graph is a directly checkable Hamiltonicity certificate. Universally, this construction gives a 2-factor with at most floor((n+4)/6)-1 cycles.

A second reduction suppresses degree-2 paths in a bichromatic dual graph. If the direct adjacency graph among its degree-at-least-3 vertices becomes a forest after deleting at most one vertex, an independent set can be chosen whose complement is an induced tree. Through duality this proves Hamiltonicity. Hence any counterexample must have at least three nonquadrilateral faces in every face-colour class, every corresponding long-face adjacency graph must have feedback-vertex number at least two, every quadrilateral auxiliary graph must be disconnected, and every bichromatic graph must fail to be series-parallel.

Combining this with exact face-length arithmetic and a classification of bipartite graphs on 3+3 vertices proves from scratch that every graph satisfying the target assumptions on at most 30 vertices is Hamiltonian. Thus these arguments alone force any counterexample to have at least 32 vertices. The stronger finite bound merely reported by the paper was not used because its certificates are not contained in the permitted input.

results.claim: The planar dual T of G is a simple Eulerian plane triangulation with a proper vertex 3-colouring I1,I2,I3, unique up to permuting the colours.
results.proof_sketch: Three-connectivity gives a polyhedral plane embedding, so facial boundaries are simple cycles and the dual is simple. Cubicity makes every dual face a triangle. Bipartiteness makes every primal face even, hence every dual vertex has even degree. The supplied paper proves that an Eulerian plane triangulation has the stated tripartition.

results.claim: For each colour i, the boundaries of the primal faces corresponding to Ii are pairwise vertex-disjoint cycles covering V(G). Moreover, each colour class has total face perimeter n=|V(G)|, G has n/2+2 faces, and it has at least six quadrilateral faces.
results.proof_sketch: At every primal vertex, the three incident faces correspond to a triangular face of T and hence have the three distinct colours. Thus exactly one face of each colour contains each primal vertex, proving the spanning 2-factor and perimeter assertions. Cubicity gives |E|=3n/2, so Euler's formula gives |F|=n/2+2. Therefore sum over faces of 6-|f| equals 6(n/2+2)-2|E|=12. All face lengths are even and at least four, so only quadrilaterals contribute positively, by 2 each; hence there are at least six.

results.claim: G is Hamiltonian if and only if V(T) can be partitioned into two sets inducing forests.
results.proof_sketch: Given such a partition X,Y, no triangular face of T is monochromatic. Each triangle consequently has exactly two X-Y edges. If N=|V(T)|, there are 2N-4 cross edges and therefore N-2 internal edges. If the two induced forests have cX,cY components, their internal-edge count is N-cX-cY, so cX=cY=1: both are trees. The primal edges dual to the cross edges have degree two at every primal vertex and form a spanning 2-factor. Its k disjoint Jordan curves divide the sphere into k+1 regions, while the two dual trees show there are exactly two regions; hence k=1. Conversely, a Hamiltonian cycle separates primal faces into inside and outside. Face adjacency within either disk is connected, and the n/2 noncycle edges give exactly N-2 internal dual edges, forcing both connected induced subgraphs to be trees.

results.claim: If any bichromatic graph H=T[Ii union Ij] has a CAI-partition, then G is Hamiltonian.
results.proof_sketch: The supplied Observation 7 makes H simple, planar, bipartite, and 2-vertex-connected. Let A union J be its CAI-partition, with T[A] a tree and J independent. Observation 6, whose planar triangle argument is supplied in the paper, shows that T[J union Ik] is a forest for the omitted colour k. Thus T is partitioned into two induced forests, and the preceding dual equivalence supplies a Hamiltonian cycle.

results.claim: In particular, G is Hamiltonian whenever some bichromatic graph T[Ii union Ij] is series-parallel.
results.proof_sketch: Such a bichromatic graph is simple and 2-vertex-connected. Theorem 10 proved in the supplied paper gives it a CAI-partition. Apply the preceding reduction.

results.claim: For distinct colours i,j, let Qij have the i-coloured faces as vertices, with one edge for every j-coloured quadrilateral joining the two i-coloured faces opposite it. Then G has a spanning 2-factor with exactly c(Qij) cycles. In particular, connected Qij certifies Hamiltonicity.
results.proof_sketch: Start with the facial 2-factor formed by boundaries of i-coloured faces. Around a j-coloured quadrilateral, edges alternately belong and do not belong to this factor; its two incident i-faces are distinct because T is simple. Faces of colour j are mutually vertex-disjoint. Choose a spanning forest S of Qij and, for every corresponding quadrilateral, take symmetric difference with its four boundary edges. Process the edges of S in forest order. Each switch removes one edge from each of two cycles corresponding to distinct current forest components and inserts the other opposite pair, merging those cycles into one. Disjointness ensures earlier switches cannot disturb a later alternating quadrilateral. Initially cycles correspond to vertices of Qij; after |V(Qij)|-c(Qij) merges, exactly c(Qij) remain.

results.claim: Every target graph on n vertices has a spanning 2-factor with at most floor((n+4)/6)-1 cycles.
results.proof_sketch: The bipartition classes have equal size, and planarity excludes the size-three case K3,3, so n>=8. Let a be the smallest number of faces in a face-colour class. Then a<=floor((n/2+2)/3)=floor((n+4)/6). If a=1, its boundary is Hamiltonian. Otherwise some other colour contains a quadrilateral: if both other classes contained none, all their faces would have length at least six, so each would have at most n/6 faces; minimality gives the same bound for a, contradicting the total n/2+2 faces. That quadrilateral is a nonloop edge of the appropriate Qij, so its spanning forest has at most a-1 components. Apply the switch construction.

results.claim: Let H be 2-vertex-connected. Suppress its maximal degree-2 paths to a multigraph K, let B be the vertices of degree at least three, and let U=H[B], the unsubdivided skeleton edges. If U is a forest, or U-v is a forest for some v in B, then H has a CAI-partition.
results.proof_sketch: If H is a cycle, remove one vertex. Otherwise, in the first case extend U to a spanning tree R of connected K. In the second, put v into the independent set; 2-connectivity makes K-v connected, so extend U-v to a spanning tree R of K-v. Every remaining skeleton edge not incident with v is subdivided, since every unsubdivided edge was put into R. From each such non-tree path choose one internal vertex for the independent set. Chosen vertices lie on distinct degree-2 paths and are mutually nonadjacent; none is adjacent to v. The intact paths representing R form a subdivided tree. Deleting the selected vertex from each other path leaves only pendant path fragments, and paths formerly incident with v also become pendant. Hence the complement is connected and acyclic, giving a CAI-partition.

results.claim: In any counterexample, every face-colour class contains at least three nonquadrilateral faces; for every colour pair, their nonquadrilateral-face adjacency graph has feedback-vertex number at least two. Moreover, every Qij is disconnected and every bichromatic graph is non-series-parallel.
results.proof_sketch: In a bichromatic graph, a vertex has degree half the corresponding primal face length, so its degree-at-least-3 vertices are precisely the nonquadrilateral faces. If one colour contributed at most two such vertices, its side of the adjacency graph would have size at most two. With fewer than two it is acyclic; with exactly two, deleting either one destroys every bipartite cycle. The skeleton lemma would give a CAI-partition and hence a Hamiltonian cycle. Thus each class has at least three and every pair has feedback-vertex number at least two. The final two conditions follow respectively from the quadrilateral-switch and series-parallel criteria.

results.claim: If two face-colour classes each consist of exactly three hexagons together with any number of quadrilaterals, then G is Hamiltonian.
results.proof_sketch: Let H be their bichromatic graph and U the adjacency graph on the six hexagon vertices, with parts of size three. If H had no CAI-partition, the skeleton lemma would imply that U-v contains a cycle for every vertex v. Deleting a vertex in one part leaves only two vertices there, so those two must have at least two common neighbours. Thus every pair of rows, and symmetrically every pair of columns, in the 3-by-3 adjacency matrix has at least two common ones. This forces at most one zero entry: row conditions put all zeros in one column, while column conditions put them in one row. Hence U is K3,3 or K3,3 minus one edge. The former is nonplanar. In the latter, four hexagon vertices already have degree three, while the missing-edge endpoints each have one unused incidence. All degree-2 vertices of H must therefore form a path joining those endpoints, making H a subdivision of K3,3, again nonplanar. Thus H has a CAI-partition and G is Hamiltonian.

results.claim: Every graph satisfying the target assumptions with at most 30 vertices is Hamiltonian; consequently these arguments force every counterexample to have at least 32 vertices.
results.proof_sketch: Write n=2m. For colour i let qi count quadrilaterals, ri nonquadrilateral faces, and si=sum(|f|/2-3) over the latter. The colour-perimeter identity gives 2qi+3ri+si=m. Summing and using q+r=m+2 yields r+s=m-4. A counterexample has ri>=3, hence r>=9. Thus m>=13. For m=13, necessarily r=9,s=0, so all three classes have exactly three hexagons. For m=14, either (r,s)=(9,1), when parity ri+si congruent to m modulo 2 would force every si odd and s>=3, or (10,0), whose (3,3,4) distribution violates the same parity; both are impossible. For m=15, the possibilities (r,s)=(9,2),(10,1),(11,0), together with parity, always leave at least two classes with (ri,si)=(3,0). Hence at m=13 or 15 two classes have exactly three hexagons and otherwise quadrilaterals, so the preceding criterion applies. Smaller m and m=14 are impossible. Therefore n<=30 is Hamiltonian; n is even, so a counterexample must have n>=32.
